scenario.title: What evidence is missing before comparing aquatic refuges?
scenario.question: We have air temperature, humidity and rainfall from NASA POWER. What would you do before deciding on the aquatic habitat?

choices.label: Use air temperature as water temperature
Pick the site with the smallest p-value
Ask for water data series and habitat evidence

scenario.feedback: Correct: still needed: sea temperature, productivity/plankton, upwelling, oxygen. Air temperature is not a substitute for sea and seabed temperature.
scenario.limitations: Complete species card and evidence exercise; there are not yet three aquatic refuge options or validated water series.

key_variables.brief_favorable_conditions: Cold, nutrient-rich currents (18–23 °C), constant upwelling of zooplankton, shallow rocky reefs.
key_variables.why_these_variables: Sea-surface temperature, El Niño-type warm peaks and winds that drive upwelling. Plankton and currents are not available.

survival_card.use_rule: Compare the same indicator, unit, annual aggregation and years. Values describe the historical regional grid cell, not measured physiological tolerances. A difference or an out-of-range value does not establish survival or death.

requirements.value: Cold upwelled water around the islands. 18–23 °C is not a measured tolerance.
requirements.evidence: The 1982–83 El Niño suppressed the cold upwelling; the fish has not been seen since 1983.
